samples.summary: Autofit-grow commit behaviour changed, but only the panel design doc was updated; the canonical autofit doc is now stale
samples.evidence: `docs/design/slides/slides-text-autofit.md:219-221` is the authoritative record for grow-mode persistence: "Height is persisted at commit ... `onCommit` writes `frame.h = max(MIN_TEXT_BOX_H, contentHeight)` via `store.updateElementFrame(...)`". This delta changes that write to also carry compensated `x`/`y` (`packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:4431-4436`), yet the only doc updated is `docs/design/slides/slides-format-options-panel.md:243-251`, a panel-scoped doc that now describes editor autofit behaviour. samples.summary: Non-finite fallback in anchoredFramePatch doesn't actually prevent garbage being persisted, and the whole `rotation ?? 0` layer defends against a state the model type forbids
samples.evidence: `if (!Number.isFinite(next.x) || !Number.isFinite(next.y)) return patch;` degrades to the size-only patch, but when the non-finite input is a NaN `w`/`h` (the case the comment cites) the returned `patch` still carries that NaN straight into `updateElementFrame`, so the "rather than writing garbage coordinates" justification only half holds — the guard buys nothing over just writing the compensated values. Combined with three fresh `start.rotation ?? 0` sites in `resize.ts` (74, 97, 155) against a field the model declares required (`packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:11`), this is a defensive layer the type system says is unreachable, only exercisable in tests via `as unknown as Frame` casts. If legacy frames really can omit `rotation`, the durable fix belongs at the load/import normalization boundary (as `import/pptx/shape.ts:1106` already does), not scattered per-callsite in an interaction module.
